---
title: 'Use a hosted catalog'
description: "Initialize, authenticate to, clone, and replay catalogs backed by the hosted Xorq blob service"
execute:
  eval: false
---

A hosted catalog keeps its reviewable manifest and content pointers in Git while the Xorq catalog service manages the referenced blobs. The Git repository contains the stable service identity; credentials stay in the runtime environment.

## Initialize a hosted catalog

Set the catalog identity and service URL supplied by the hosted service:

```bash
export XORQ_CONTENT_STORE_PRESIGNED_CATALOG_ID=11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
export XORQ_CONTENT_STORE_PRESIGNED_SERVICE_URL=https://catalog.example/
```

Then initialize the catalog with its hosted Git remote:

```bash
xorq catalog --path ./analytics-catalog init \
  --content-store presigned \
  --remote-url https://catalog.example/acme/analytics.git
```

`--remote-url` is required and must be the catalog's only remote, with an `owner/slug.git` path below the configured service URL. Do not put credentials in it.

`--content-store` reads its settings from the process environment, not from `--env-file` (which configures an annex remote instead). Export the two variables above, or source a file that does, before running `init`.

If Git is configured with a `url.<base>.insteadOf` rewrite that covers the service, the rewritten URL is what gets validated, and a hosted catalog whose rewritten remote leaves the service URL is rejected.

Initialization commits only `catalog_id` and `service_url` in `content_store.yaml`:

```yaml
type: presigned
catalog_id: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
service_url: https://catalog.example/
```

Tokens, object-store locations, signed URLs, and cloud credentials are not part of the committed configuration.

## Authenticate at runtime

For private reads and all writes, provide the short-lived bearer token issued by the service:

```bash
export XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN='your-short-lived-token'
export XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN_SERVICE_URL=https://catalog.example/
```

Xorq reads `XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN` for each hosted blob request, so a refreshed token takes effect without changing or recreating the catalog. `XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN_SERVICE_URL` scopes that credential to one hosted service; Xorq will not send it to a catalog on another origin or base path. The token is never written to Git and is not sent to the signed object-storage URL. Public downloads can work without a token when the service permits anonymous access.

`XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN` is not passed to Git. Configure Git separately to use the catalog token as the HTTP Basic password, for example with `x-access-token` as the username, through a credential helper or prompt. Never embed it in the remote URL.

## Clone and use the catalog

With any required Git credential configured, clone the hosted URL normally:

```bash
git clone https://catalog.example/acme/analytics.git
xorq catalog --path ./analytics list
```

Xorq detects `content_store.yaml` and uses the hosted blob client automatically. Export `XORQ_CATALOG_TOKEN` before an operation that needs authenticated blob access.

## Replay into a hosted catalog

Provide the target remote along with the hosted content-store configuration:

```bash
xorq catalog --path ./source-catalog replay ./hosted-copy \
  --content-store presigned \
  --remote-url https://catalog.example/acme/hosted-copy.git
```

Non-dry-run replay requires `--remote-url` and configures it before uploading. A dry run creates no target and needs no remote.

## Blob lifecycle

Removing an entry deletes only its Git-tracked pointer. Hosted blob collection is server-owned, so `xorq catalog gc` is unavailable for hosted catalogs.
